_doc: The same lexicon as contracts/lexicon.json (v2.4: every rule, cue and pattern identical; tests/test_brief.py fails if they drift), with the competitor list of a real travel-and-expense market instead of the demo's three invented names. Select it with the LEXICON_PATH environment variable, e.g. LEXICON_PATH=contracts/lexicon.travel-expense.json (an absolute path, or relative to where the run starts); without it the demo lexicon loads and demo outputs are unchanged. Findings and the brief are stamped with this file's version (2.4-travel-expense). Names that are also everyday words carry competitor_rules: Ramp ('ramp up', 'ramp-up', 'on-ramp', 'ramping'), Concur ('I concur', 'we concur', 'concur with', a sentence that is only 'Concur.'), Perk ('perk of', 'a perk', 'perks', 'perk up'), Center ('cost center', 'data center', 'call center', 'center of', and place names such as 'Medical Center' or 'Convention Center'), Airbase (an air base), all case-sensitive; Concur and Perk exclude only as written ('We use Concur with our cards' and 'a Perk trial' are the products). 'Amex' alone is the card issuer, not a competitor: only 'Amex GBT', 'American Express Global Business Travel' or 'Egencia' count, as Amex GBT. Brex, Pleo, Coupa, Spotnana, Expensify, Emburse, Spendesk and Rippling Spend are distinctive and match in any case. The list is the market as publicly described in 2026; a team edits it to its own competitors in a reviewed commit. The evaluation sets were labelled against the demo names, so this list has no precision or recall figure; tests/test_brief_eval.py checks only that, on all 360 evaluation rows, it fires on the two rows that write a real name (Concur) and never on 'cost center' or 'Amex' rows.

competitor_rules._doc: How a team lists its own competitors: add each name to 'competitors', then add a rule here when the name is also an everyday word or the company has other names. case_sensitive: true matches only the name as written (so 'I concur' is not Concur, 'a nice perk' is not Perk). exclude: phrases that contain the name but are not the competitor; a match inside one is ignored ('ramp up' is not Ramp, 'cost center' is not Center). Excluded phrases match in any case, or, with exclude_match_case: true, only as written (a capital first letter allowed at the start of a sentence), so 'Concur with that.' is the verb while 'we use Concur with our cards' is the product. aliases: other names, any case, reported under the listed name ('SAP Concur' is Concur, 'Egencia' is Amex GBT). A name with no rule matches as a whole word in any case. Example for real names: {"Ramp": {"case_sensitive": true, "exclude": ["ramp up", "ramp-up", "on-ramp"]}, "Concur": {"case_sensitive": true, "exclude_match_case": true, "exclude": ["I concur", "we concur", "concur with"]}, "Center": {"case_sensitive": true, "exclude": ["cost center", "call center", "data center"]}}. The full worked list is contracts/lexicon.travel-expense.json.

pricing._doc: Pricing friction = pushback on OUR price, fees, contract or terms, not the customer's own spend. It counts when (a) a standalone phrase matches, (b) a price term and a friction cue sit within within_words words of each other in the same sentence, or (c) a comparison puts our price above another offer in a sentence anchored to us (anchors_us): a comparison_priced phrase ('more expensive than', 'costs more than'), or a comparison phrase ('higher than', 'double what') within within_words words of a price term. 'Higher than yours' favours us and does not match; a not_price phrase ('approval rates', 'adoption rate') or a benefit ('rebates', where higher favours us) is not a price term for (c). A sentence about the customer's travel spend (travel_spend: travel budget, hotels, airfare, flights, per diem, rates in <City>) does not count unless it is anchored to us (anchors_us: your price, the licence, per seat, the quote, the proposal, the renewal number, the subscription). 'negated' turns ('price is not the issue') never count. v2.3: contract-length terms ('a three year term', 'out clause') are terms, and 'non-starter', 'deal-breaker' and 'doesn't make sense' are friction cues; 'more than we budgeted' and 'over what we planned' are standalone. v2.4: comparisons (c).

timing_window._doc: A month, quarter or date alone is not a timing window ('We hired three new people in March'). A 'when' match counts only if a 'context' word (decision, contract, RFP, budget cycle, go-live, notice, signing, procurement) is within within_words words in the same sentence. 'customer_context' (renewal words) counts only in a customer's own words: the CRM already holds the renewal date. v2.3: a bare 'deadline' or 'freeze' is not context (an expense deadline, a travel or hiring freeze are the customer's own operations; a budget freeze still is); procurement (the process, not a job title such as 'procurement lead' or 'head of procurement'), purchase paperwork (paperwork, PO, order form, MSA) and 'make a call' are. Month abbreviations (not 'mar', 'may') and holidays name a date.

expansion_negated._doc: An expansion hit does not count when a negation sits just before it ('not looking to expand', 'we don't need more seats'), or when it is past tense and the text says there are no plans for more ('We expanded into Mexico last year, no plans for more'): that is history, not a request.

observer_cues._doc: Observer check (gtm_briefs.observer.validate): a theme the model proposes is kept only if its verbatim evidence contains one of these words for THAT theme. Broad on purpose (not the lexicon patterns): it stops 'the product' being accepted as pricing evidence. A trailing * matches any ending (licen* = licence, licensing); otherwise the whole word. Timing evidence may also name a month, quarter or date (timing_window.when). Competitor evidence must contain a listed competitor name. v2.3: timing cues are purchase words only (a date is accepted only when the sentence holding it has one); expansion cues point at more of OUR product (seats, users, licences, modules, tier, rollout, add, expand, want it), not the customer's own growth (headcount, hiring, a new office).

observer_not._doc: Observer check: a proposed theme is refused when its verbatim evidence matches this pattern. A request for content, or our team sending it, is not engagement yet (nothing was read, watched or used).
observer_not.engagement: \b(send me|send us|send (it|that|them) over|could you send|can you send|please send|per (her|his|their) request|asked (us )?for|request(ed|ing)?)\b

gong_trackers._doc: Gong tracker name -> theme. A tracker hit inside a customer's turn adds that theme (Gong matched it; the confidence rules still apply). Use your own tracker names.
